fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Detached Structure; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the road entrance to the access drive so responders can locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the edge of the access drive, particularly where dense vegetation narrows the opening.
• Trim back vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain a clear path wide enough for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back any tree branches hanging over the access drive to maintain overhead clearance for fire and rescue vehicles.
• Create a designated turnaround area near the main residence or detached structure so emergency vehicles are not required to back out to the road.
• Keep the turnaround area clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials at all times.
• Trim shrubs and vegetation growing close to the main residence so responders can move around the exterior of the structure without obstruction.
• Trim shrubs and vegetation growing close to the detached structure so responders can access all sides.
• Cut back dense vegetation adjacent to both structures to reduce the risk of fire spreading directly to the buildings.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings.
• If a gate is present at the access drive entrance, keep it unlocked or install a Knox Box so responders can enter without delay.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Mixed Vegetation; Limited Vegetation Separation; Scattered Shrubs; Open Clearing; Long Driveway; Vegetation Along Driveway; Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back all shrubs and low branches that are touching or within a few feet of the house walls.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open gaps between the canopy and the roofline.
• Remove low-hanging branches from trees closest to the house so flames cannot climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Separate the scattered shrubs from nearby trees so fire cannot move easily between them.
• Clear ground vegetation and dead plant material from directly around the base of the house.
• Mow or cut down tall grass and low ground cover in the open clearing to keep it from carrying fire toward the structure.
• Thin the mixed vegetation on all sides of the house to create open space between plants and the building.
• Trim overhanging branches along the full length of the driveway so vehicles, including fire trucks, can pass through without obstruction.
• Clear shrubs and tall vegetation growing along the edges of the driveway to keep sight lines open and reduce fire exposure along the travel path.
• Remove any dead or dry plant material from the vegetation growing along the driveway.
• Keep the ground along the driveway mowed or cleared so fire cannot run along the roadside toward the house.
• Thin scattered trees around the structure to break up the continuous tree cover surrounding the house.
